concept.name: Dark cloud cover
concept.definition: A two-candlestick pattern in an uptrend: a long white candle is followed by a black candle that opens above the prior high (ideally with a gap) and closes more than halfway down into the prior white body. Technical analysts read it as a potential top reversal signal, the bearish mirror of the piercing line and a weaker cousin of the bearish engulfing pattern.
concept.intuition: Buyers gapped the market up at the open, but sellers dragged price back down through more than half of the previous session's gains, casting a dark cloud over the rally.
concept.mechanics: From OHLC data: candle 1 is a long white body; candle 2 opens at or above H1 and closes below the midpoint (O1 + C1) / 2 of the first body but above O1 (otherwise it would be a bearish engulfing). Deeper penetration of the first body strengthens the conventional bearish reading.
concept.formula: Dark cloud cover when C1 > O1, O2 >= H1, and O1 < C2 < (O1 + C1)/2.
concept.failure_modes: Shallow penetration (barely past the midpoint) frequently fails, particularly in strong uptrends where the dip is bought. In gapless 24-hour markets the opening-gap condition is usually relaxed, weakening selectivity.
concept.misconceptions: If the second candle closes below the first candle's open, the pattern is a bearish engulfing, not dark cloud cover. The name refers only to the partial-penetration configuration, and confirmation is still required.
concept.example: A stock rises, printing a candle from 60.00 open to 62.00 close (high 62.20). The next day opens at 62.50 and closes at 60.50, below the 61.00 midpoint of the prior body: dark cloud cover, read as a warning of an impending top.
